fixed_before: any Stage 3 result. Do not change it after seeing results; a change is a new version.
applies_to: course runs (no --pairs) with a neutral prompt. --pairs benchmark runs never use it.

rule.direction reverses: both directions proposed to the validator, order_agreement = reversed; never pick one automatically

link_fields: Strength and confidence come from the ask that proposed the link; when both did, from the hash-order ask, which is what a one-order run would have used. Evidence is the union of what both asks cited, hash-order ask first.
reasoning: From the 30 non-gold sample pairs of cdlp/discovery/results/order_bias_ds101.json: 20 said NEITHER both ways, 1 gave the same link both ways, 7 gave a link in one order only (3 of them in the hash order) and 2 reversed. One order would keep or lose a link, or fix its direction, on the hash alone. Asking both ways keeps every link for the validator, marks how stable it was, and leaves a reversal for a teacher.
also_seen: The 5 positive ds101 gold pairs were also seen when choosing this rule; see cdlp/discovery/results/README.md.
